title: Mastering Marfan Syndrome: Ocular Manifestations & Management
summary: Marfan syndrome is an autosomal dominant connective tissue disorder caused by FBN1 mutations, significantly impacting the ocular, cardiovascular, and skeletal systems. Early recognition of ectopia lentis is crucial for preventing life-threatening complications.

sections.title: Definition & Pathophysiology
sections.content: Marfan syndrome is a systemic connective tissue disorder due to mutations in the FBN1 gene (15q21.1) encoding fibrillin-1. Pathophysiology involves defective microfibril formation, leading to TGF-beta dysregulation, causing weakened elastic fibers in the zonules, aortic media, and joint capsules.

sections.title: Ocular Manifestations
content: Increased risk of Rhegmatogenous Retinal Detachment

content.explanation: M: Mitral valve prolapse, A: Aortic root dilation, R: Retinal detachment, F: Fibrillin, A: Arachnodactyly, N: Negative lens displacement (inferior in homocystinuria), S: Striae

sections.title: Management Strategy
content: Step 1: Annual ophthalmic exam (Refraction, slit-lamp, fundus).
Step 2: Beta-blockers or ARBs (Losartan) to slow aortic root growth.
Step 3: Surgical intervention (Lens extraction if visual axis is obscured).
Step 4: Prophylactic laser retinopexy for high-risk peripheral retinal degeneration.

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls
content: Ectopia lentis in Marfan usually displaces superotemporally due to weak superior zonules.
Homocystinuria presents with downward lens subluxation and should be ruled out via metabolic screening (urinary cyanide-nitroprusside test).
Avoid pilocarpine in lens subluxation as it induces miosis and potentially pupillary block if the lens is mobile.
Marfan patients undergoing cataract surgery are at high risk for zonular dialysis; consider capsular tension rings (CTR) or iris-claw intraocular lenses.
